Excludes time spent in permission prompts and PreToolUse hooks", so deriving PreToolUse-hook-added latency from it would indeed read near-zero. VERDICT_PLAN.md:277 says what is quoted, and `verdicts.latency_ms` already exists in the plan's schema (:109). The recommendation is the right fix. Two refinements worth noting: self-timestamping inside the hook process misses Claude Code's own process-spawn overhead, so pair it with a wall-clock comparison (e.g. a with/without-plugin run) for the true "added latency" figure; and the field is also marked Optional, so it can be absent entirely.

findings.title: Section 3.2's sessions table (started_at/ended_at/outcome) has no hook wired to populate it, and SessionEnd cannot make decisions
findings.problem: The plan's `sessions` table wants `started_at`, `ended_at`, and `outcome`, but the phased build plan (Section 6) never adds a SessionStart or SessionEnd hook -- only PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop/SubagentStop are mentioned. SessionEnd is the natural place to close `ended_at`, but it has no decision control at all (can't block, and its JSON output including `systemMessage` is discarded), so it is cleanup-only and must fit the real 1.5s budget from CC-3.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:107: '`sessions(id, started_at, ended_at, cwd_hash, model, plugin_version, forced_continuations, outcome)`'. 'SessionEnd hooks have no decision control. They can't block session termination but can perform cleanup tasks. Claude Code discards their JSON output fields, such as `systemMessage`.' -- cc_hooks.md:3352.
findings.recommendation: Add SessionStart (to open a `sessions` row and read `source`/`model`) and SessionEnd (to close `ended_at`, within the 1.5s budget) hooks explicitly to Section 4/6's phase plan, and note in Section 3.2 that SessionEnd cannot set `outcome` interactively -- `outcome` must come from the Stop verifier's last verdict or an external test-runner signal instead.

verifier.note: cc_hooks.md:3352 is verbatim ("SessionEnd hooks have no decision control ... Claude Code discards their JSON output fields, such as `systemMessage`"), and VERDICT_PLAN.md:107 has the sessions table as quoted. I grepped the whole plan: SessionStart and SessionEnd appear nowhere, and Phase 2 (:214) lists only `verdict hook pre|post|stop|subagent-stop`, so the gap is real. Two corrections to the recommendation. (a) SessionStart fires on more than session creation — cc_hooks.md:1155 lists `source` values `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, and `fork`, so "open a sessions row" on every SessionStart would create several rows per session_id; it must be an upsert. (b) cc_hooks.md:1153 says `model` is optional and "can be omitted, for example after `/clear` or when a session is restored through conversation recovery", so the schema's `model` column must be nullable and backfillable.
verifier.corrected_recommendation: Add SessionStart and SessionEnd command hooks to Sections 4 and 6. SessionStart should UPSERT the `sessions` row keyed on `session_id` (it fires again on `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, and `fork` — cc_hooks.md:1155) and treat `model` as optional (cc_hooks.md:1153), backfilling it later from a hook input that has it. SessionEnd closes `ended_at` only, as cleanup: it cannot block and its JSON output, `systemMessage` included, is discarded (cc_hooks.md:3352), and as a PLUGIN-provided hook it is pinned to the 1.5s budget because plugin hook timeouts don't raise it (cc_hooks.md:3354) — so it must be a stdlib-only single UPDATE. Note in Section 3.2 that `outcome` comes from the Stop verifier's last verdict or an external test-runner signal, never from SessionEnd.

COMP.summary: The seven prior reviews are individually strong but collectively unusable: they issue mutually exclusive instructions (JSONL vs SQLite, cut-the-dashboard vs harden-the-dashboard, 120 labels vs 1000, drop-PreToolUse vs harden-PreToolUse, cut-telemetry vs fix-telemetry) and the plan has no artifact recording which side won. An agent handed the plan plus seven review blobs will pick arbitrarily per session and silently regress. The largest gap is not technical: Section 0 rule 6 gestures at docs/DECISIONS.md and Section 5 says CLAUDE.md is generated from this doc, i.e. from the document the reviewers just falsified. Whole areas are untouched by every reviewer: uninstall and upgrade behavior, a supported-platform statement, a kill switch, the hook.log format the plan names once and never defines, a doctor command, the fixture-capture and run-one-hook-by-hand developer loop, cost ceilings beyond the $40 judge baseline, and the token tax Verdict imposes on the user's own Claude context. Two load-bearing premises remain unmeasured: no API key exists on this machine, so every latency number is secondhand from jev-belay or modeled, and the context budget is contradicted between VERIFIED_FACTS (32,000 tokens, authoritative and smaller) and PRIOR-5 (64K). I verified locally that the PATH python3 (3.14.7) fails TLS certificate verification against api.typesafe.ai while /usr/bin/python3 (3.9.6) succeeds, a concrete instance of the silent-failure mode nobody specified detection for, since fail-open plus exit 0 makes a Verdict that never reaches the provider indistinguishable from one passing everything. Every fix below is a paragraph, a command or a table, and all belong in the plan before Phase 0.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md is specified as generate-from-this-doc, i.e. from the document seven reviewers just falsified
findings.problem: The only instruction for the project CLAUDE.md is a comment in the repo-layout tree. An agent following it regenerates the refuted assumptions: PostToolUse sees failures, permissionDecision allow is legal output, the transcript is the Stop input, stderr surfaces a flag, Stop has a 1.5s budget, jev-latest is the model id, SQLAlchemy is fine in a hook. Section 0 rule 3 also points at a different hooks URL than the one facts were verified against. Nothing says VERIFIED_FACTS.md exists or outranks the plan, and nothing carries forward the no-invented-fields rule this review cycle exists because of.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:169 'CLAUDE.md  # project instructions for Claude Code (generate from this doc)'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:16 'Claude Code hooks: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/hooks' vs VERIFIED_FACTS.md:5 'cc_hooks.md = https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md'
findings.recommendation: Add Section 0.6 listing seven required CLAUDE.md blocks, written before Phase 0 code. (1) Precedence line: docs/VERIFIED_FACTS.md > docs/DECISIONS.md > VERDICT_PLAN.md; copy VERIFIED_FACTS.md into the repo in Phase 0. (2) A NEVER REINTRODUCE table, one row per wrong belief with correction and citation: PostToolUse sees failures (no, PostToolUseFailure, VERIFIED_FACTS.md:13); emitting permissionDecision allow (no, SEC-1); transcript parsing in the hot path (no, last_assistant_message, VERIFIED_FACTS.md:17); stderr shows a flag on allow-stop (no, systemMessage, CC-2); Stop must finish in 1.5s (no, that is SessionEnd, CC-3); jev-latest (no, pinned id per provider, EVAL-12); pydantic/SQLAlchemy/httpx/yaml under plugin/hot (no, 154 ms, VERIFIED_FACTS.md:36); the 68% figure and the hello@typesafe.ai showcase program (no source, LEGAL-3). (3) Citation rule verbatim: never state an API field, flag or clause you have not read in a source this session; cite file:line or a fetched URL, else write unverified and stop. (4) Correct doc URLs code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md and /plugins-reference.md. (5) Pointer to docs/FINDINGS_LEDGER.md. (6) The per-phase gate commands copied inline. (7) Hot-path invariants: exit 0 always; never hold a write transaction across a network call; no non-stdlib import under plugin/hot.

findings.title: No mechanism records which reviewer won: five pairs of findings are mutually exclusive
findings.problem: Section 0 rule 6 asks for a log of non-obvious choices, but the reviews produced contradictions: SEQ-2 deletes SQLite from the hook path while DB-1 specifies WAL pragmas for concurrent SQLite hook processes; SCOPE-2 deletes the dashboard while SEC-9 hardens it and EVAL-8 requires a blinded label mode inside it; SCOPE-2 deletes telemetry while SEC-12 and LEGAL-12 rewrite it; PRIOR-11 says lock agent-verdict while NAME-1 says rename everything to one string; line 375 makes Stop blocking possibly opt-in while 4.3 blocks by default and CFG-1 adds off/shadow/enforce with no stated default.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:19 'Keep a docs/DECISIONS.md log. One entry per non-obvious choice (why SQLite locally, why this compression strategy, etc.).'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:375 'make Stop blocking opt-in for the first release if dogfooding shows friction'
findings.recommendation: Insert Phase -1 (half a day) producing docs/FINDINGS_LEDGER.md: one row per finding id from all eight reviews with columns id, lens, severity, disposition (Applied/Rejected/Deferred-v2), plan section rewritten, one-line rationale. Add tests/test_ledger.py asserting every id appears once with a disposition, wired into make check. Resolve these five there: (a) storage, Apply SEQ-2 and Reject DB-1's concurrency pragmas as moot, since one append-only JSONL writer per process removes the concurrent-writer problem, keeping DB-1's payload caps and prune command; (b) dashboard, Apply SCOPE-2's verdict report --out report.html plus a terminal verdict label, carrying SEC-9's escaping into the HTML writer and EVAL-8's blinding into verdict label as a default-on --blinded flag; (c) telemetry, Apply the v1 cut and Defer SEC-12 and LEGAL-12; (d) name, Apply NAME-1, one identical string across PyPI, repo, plugin.json and marketplace; (e) default mode, ship mode: shadow at v1.0 and flip to enforce only after the eval report exists.

findings.title: Whether Section 4.1 ships in v1 is unresolved across four findings, and the product's one-sentence pitch depends on it
findings.problem: PRIOR-1 drops the Jev dangerous question as redundant; SCOPE-1 schedules PreToolUse only if an earlier block finishes early; DATA-1 says dangerous has no reachable real positives and must be synthetic-only; SEC-1 and SEC-2 assume it ships and harden it; JEV-1 keeps it behind a prefilter. Nobody states the consequence: cutting PreToolUse Jev changes the product sentence, the definition of done, the launch title, the resume bullet and the dangerous rows of the eval. An agent builds whichever version the section it is reading implies, and the README ends up contradicting the code.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:28 'A Claude Code plugin that catches agents lying about success, blocks dangerous actions, and shows you a calibration-backed dashboard of how trustworthy your agent actually is.'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:32 'Hooks: PreToolUse safety gate, PostToolUse failure recorder, Stop/SubagentStop completion verifier.'
findings.recommendation: Resolve as: v1 ships PreToolUse deterministic-only, no Jev call. Keep SEC-2's Layer 1 denylist and SEC-1's never-emit-allow rule; delete destructive, in_scope and touches_secrets from Section 4.1 and policies/default.yaml; delete the dangerous row from the 8.1 targets and 8.2 metrics; move the Jev gate to Section 15 as extension 6 with PRIOR-1's acceptance test attached (ships only if it beats a bundled rule pack on the same gold set). Rewrite line 28 to: a Claude Code plugin that catches agents claiming success their tool output does not support, records every tool failure by exit code, and publishes a calibrated reproducible measurement of how often that happens. Rewrite line 32's first clause to PreToolUse deterministic denylist (no model call), and update the Section 13 bullet and the Show HN title in the same commit.

findings.title: Gold-set scale is specified three incompatible ways and no reviewer set the publication gate that reconciles them
findings.problem: The plan wants 300 hand labels with 60 positives per key; EVAL-1 raises the publication floor to 600/150 and 1000/200 for any head-to-head claim; DATA-1 says 300 is unreachable and substitutes proxy labels plus a 120-stop audit; SCOPE-1 budgets about 98 hours. These cannot all hold, and the likely outcome is the worst one: collect what is possible, then fill in the Section 13 precision/recall/F1 bullet anyway, because that bullet is still in the plan as a template with blanks.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:263 'Targets for v1 report: >=300 manually labeled real events; >=60 positives for each of unreported_failure, claims_supported(negative class), dangerous; >=500 synthetic.'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:361 'Measured on a 300-event hand-labeled gold set: X% precision / Y% recall on unreported failures, ECE Z; 40-100x cheaper and faster than LLM-judge baselines at comparable F1'
findings.recommendation:
Adopt DATA-1's collection design as the plan and EVAL-1's numbers as gates encoded in code. In eval/report.py add PUBLICATION_GATES and emit three tiers: Tier 1 (any n) AUROC and reliability diagram with a stratified item-bootstrap 95% CI and calibrated-null band, always labelled pilot; Tier 2 (n>=600 real labeled events, >=150 positives for that key) per-question precision/recall/F1 at the shipped threshold; Tier 3 (n>=1000, >=200 positives) any between-system comparison, Pareto ranking, or the words better/outperforms. Below a tier print 'gate not met: n=, positives=

, required ' in place of the number. Delete the blanks at line 361 now, replacing them with: published a pre-registered reproducible calibration measurement on N=__ labeled stops with bootstrap confidence intervals.

findings.title: Every latency and cost number is secondhand or modeled: no API key exists and no phase gate forces a measurement
findings.problem: The PreToolUse feasibility case, the 600 ms budget, the 550 ms client deadline, the fail-open design and the cost-per-session figure all rest on roughly 250 ms p50 / 430 ms p90 Jev inference, imported from jev-belay's published end-to-end numbers rather than measured here, with no key configured. Phase 0's acceptance is a single sub-1s check on an unspecified payload, which cannot distinguish a 900 ms provider from a 250 ms one, so real latency lands after the hook design is already written.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED_FACTS.md:10 'No TYPESAFE/OPENROUTER/ANTHROPIC API key is set yet.'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:202 'Accept: smoke script returns typed answers in <1s; CI green on empty test suite.'
findings.recommendation: Replace the Phase 0 acceptance with a measurement gate that also decides scope: scripts/smoke_jev.py --n 30 --provider typesafe --provider openrouter --questions 5 --state-tokens 1200 --json reports conn_setup_ms and inference_ms separately at p50/p90/p99 per provider on a realistic Stop-shaped payload, writes raw rows to docs/measurements/phase0-<date>.json and appends a DECISIONS.md entry. Then three automatic rules: p90 end-to-end above 1200 ms on the better provider makes the Stop verifier async-record-only for v1 with blocking deferred; above 600 ms cuts any future PreToolUse Jev call; the lower-p90 provider becomes the documented default base_url. Re-run it as make bench-provider nightly, and cite docs/measurements/ rather than jev-belay in every latency claim in the report and blog.

findings.title: Context budget is provider-dependent and the authoritative fact contradicts the reviewer who corrected it
findings.problem: The plan budgets state against about 32K and compresses to 20K. PRIOR-5 calls that wrong, claims 64K total with 32K for state, and recommends re-deriving the compression budget upward. The orchestrator's verified fact records the served model's context as 32,000 tokens, which is authoritative and smaller. Re-deriving upward would silently overflow one of the two shipped providers, and the failure mode is a provider-side rejection inside a Stop hook, i.e. a fail-open pass at exactly the moment the check matters.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED_FACTS.md:32 'models typesafe/jev-1.13 (canonical typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917) and alias ~typesafe/jev-latest; context 32,000 tokens'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:50 'Context budget ~= 32K tokens shared by state + questions. Trace compression is mandatory (Section 4.3).'
findings.recommendation: Reject PRIOR-5's re-derivation for v1 and budget against the minimum across shipped providers. In policies/default.yaml add max_state_tokens: 22000 and provider_context_limit: 32000, commented with VERIFIED_FACTS.md:32 and a note that the 64K claim is unverified against the served model. In compress.py assert rendered state plus serialized questions stays under max_state_tokens, and on overflow drop oldest ok ledger rows then truncate user_task, never error rows, recording compression_overflow=1. Add a property test over a synthetic 200K-token transcript asserting the assert never fires and error rows always survive. Record response usage input tokens on every row and have verdict report print observed p99 input tokens; revisit 64K only after a real response shows more than 32,000 accepted.

findings.title: Verdict has no observability of itself: hook.log is named once and never specified, and there is no doctor command
findings.problem: Every review pushes toward exit 0 on all paths and fail-open on error. That is right for availability and catastrophic for diagnosis: a Verdict whose provider call never succeeds looks exactly like one where nothing is wrong. The plan's only instrumentation is an undefined log path. I reproduced this failure class on this machine: the interpreter first on PATH cannot complete a TLS handshake to the provider host while the Apple stock interpreter can, so the install-time probe can pick right or wrong and nothing afterward reports which.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:213 'fail-open on any exception (log to ~/.verdict/hook.log)'; verified this session: /usr/bin/python3 (3.9.6) printed 'TLS OK 3.9.6 240 ms' against api.typesafe.ai while /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.14/bin/python3 printed 'TLS FAIL 3.14.7 SSLCertVerificationError [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate'
findings.recommendation: Specify hook.log as JSON Lines with a fixed schema and cap: one object per invocation with ts, schema_v, event, session_id, prompt_id, tool_use_id, tool_name, gate_reason, provider, conn_setup_ms, inference_ms, total_ms, outcome (ok|skipped|timeout|provider_error|exception|disabled), err_class, decision, never tool content or key material; rotate at 10 MB keeping one hook.log.1. Ship verdict doctor as a Phase 2 gate printing and exiting non-zero on: resolved interpreter path and version; a live TLS handshake to the configured base_url with measured ms; whether a key is present (the word present/absent, never the value); whether plugin hooks are registered and whether a stale verdict init block sits in ~/.claude/settings.json; whether the data dir is writable at mode 0700; and the last 7 days of hook.log by outcome with the share of eligible calls that reached the provider. Add verdict doctor --audit exiting 1 on any hook exit code other than 0 or 2 (VERIFIED_FACTS.md:21) and make it the first README troubleshooting step.

findings.title: Uninstall, upgrade and a kill switch are absent from the plan and from all seven reviews
findings.problem: verdict init merges hook config into the user's settings and nothing removes it; a user who deletes the package is left with hook entries pointing at a missing executable, which per the exit-code contract prints a visible error notice on every tool call. Plugin updates relocate the install directory, so anything baking an absolute path breaks on the next update. There is no schema-upgrade story beyond one reviewer's spool-on-unknown-version rule, no downgrade path, and no way to switch Verdict off mid-session without editing config, which is the first thing anyone does when a safety plugin misfires during real work.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:215 'plugin/: manifest, hooks config, verdict init command that writes/merges hook config, README with 3-line install.'; VERIFIED_FACTS.md:27 'Env vars for hook processes: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT (install dir; changes on update; ephemeral)'
findings.recommendation: Add Section 5.1 Lifecycle with four items. (1) VERDICT_DISABLE=1 checked as the first statement of the hot path, before any import beyond os and before any I/O: exit 0 immediately; document it beside the install command and test that no rows are written and no socket opens. (2) verdict uninstall removes only the entries it wrote, tagged at write time with a _verdict key holding the version string, then prints the data path and the exact verdict purge --all command and never deletes data itself. (3) UPGRADING.md with one rule: the on-disk format carries schema_v, a newer schema_v than the running code makes the hot path spool to a pending file instead of writing, and verdict migrate is the only thing that raises it; add a CI job installing the previous tag, writing rows, upgrading, and asserting old rows still read and settings.json holds exactly one Verdict hook block. (4) Never store CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT in a path; store only the resolved interpreter path and have SessionStart re-validate and repair it.

findings.title: No supported-platform statement, yet every measurement and several design choices are macOS-arm64-only
findings.problem: The plan never says which operating systems v1 supports. Startup measurements, TLS timings, the interpreter probe order, Keychain storage for the sensitive option and the POSIX shell shim are all macOS- or POSIX-specific, and a reviewer already noted shell-form hook commands fail differently per OS. A Windows user installing from the marketplace gets a silent no-op or an error notice on every tool call, with no statement telling them not to, no Linux CI evidence, and no guard.
findings.evidence: VERIFIED_FACTS.md:10 'Machine: macOS arm64, Python 3.14 system / uv 0.12.5, Claude Code 2.1.278, docker, node 22, gh authenticated.'; VERIFIED_FACTS.md:36 '## D. Measured on this machine (Python 3.13 venv, median of 10 cold process starts)'
findings.recommendation: Add one line to README, CLAUDE.md and the plugin.json description: supported on macOS (arm64, x86_64) and Linux; Windows is untested and unsupported in v1 and Verdict disables itself there. Implement it literally: the hot path exits 0 when os.name is nt after writing one hook.log line with outcome disabled, and verdict init refuses with a one-line message. Run the hook contract tests on a CI matrix of macos-latest and ubuntu-latest and publish per-platform cold-start medians rather than one number. Make the interpreter probe platform-conditional, since /usr/bin/python3 is a macOS fact: probe VERDICT_PYTHON, then python3 on PATH, then /usr/bin/python3, requiring each candidate to pass the COMP-7 TLS handshake before it is recorded. Note in docs/PRIVACY.md that the sensitive option lands in the macOS Keychain on macOS and in the credentials file elsewhere.

findings.title: The developer loop is undefined: no Makefile targets, no fixture-capture command, no way to run one hook by hand, no cheap real-session test
findings.problem: The Makefile is one comment in a tree diagram and make eval is the only target ever named, though Section 0 rule 7 makes every metric depend on a command. The recorder phase a reviewer added describes capturing real hook stdin as prose, with no command and no redaction step, so the fixtures the whole test suite depends on have no reproducible provenance. Nothing documents feeding one JSON payload to one hook and reading the exit code, the most common debugging action here, so every session reinvents it by running a whole Claude session.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:171 'Makefile  # dev, test, eval, dashboard, docker targets'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:20 'Every metric in Section 8 must be reproducible by one command (make eval). If it is not scriptable, it is not a metric.'
findings.recommendation: Add Section 5.2 enumerating the Makefile: setup, check (ruff, mypy, the hot-path import-ban AST test, the ledger test), test, test-fast, bench-hook, bench-provider, capture-fixtures, replay, eval, eval-guard, freeze-reporting-set, report, doctor, e2e-cheap, clean. Add docs/DEVELOPING.md with three recipes. Run one hook by hand: VERDICT_DB=$(mktemp -d)/v.db plugin/hot/verdict-hook < tests/fixtures/hooks/post_fail.json then echo the exit code, the event coming from the payload's hook_event_name so one line works for every fixture. Capture fixtures: make capture-fixtures sets a temp HOME, runs claude --plugin-dir ./plugin -p over each task in scripts/capture_tasks.sh against the record-only build, then redacts and writes tests/fixtures/hooks/<event>.json plus a PROVENANCE line recording the Claude Code version (2.1.278) and date, with make check warning when a fixture's recorded version differs from the running one. Cheap E2E: make e2e-cheap runs claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events --plugin-dir ./plugin --max-turns 3 on a task designed to fail, piped to a small asserter, asserting only on synchronous hooks since async hooks are killed at teardown under -p.

findings.title: Cost ceilings exist only for the judge baseline, and the token tax Verdict imposes on the user's own context is never counted
findings.problem: One reviewer capped judge baselines at $40; nothing bounds development Jev spend, repeated eval runs across arms and providers, the proxy labeler over roughly a thousand stops, or the playground's daily ceiling, specified as a concept with no number. Separately the cheapest-looking feature is the most expensive for users: additionalContext on every PostToolUse injects Verdict's text into the user's context window on every tool call, and every Stop block re-enters as a reason the model reads on continuation. That is real money and context pressure on someone who installed a tool sold at $0.042 per million tokens, and it appears in no metric.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:135 'Optionally return additionalContext to Claude: Verdict: tool call #17 appears to have failed (p=0.91). Do not report it as successful without addressing it.'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:278 'Cost: $/session and $/1K tool calls (input tokens x $0.042/M).'
findings.recommendation: Add Section 8.6 Budget as a table of named caps with an abort in each harness: development provider spend $15 total, tracked by summing the OpenRouter usage cost field into a local counter that verdict doctor prints; eval Jev spend $25 per published report; proxy labeling $20 (Haiku over the full set, Sonnet over a fixed subsample); judge baselines $40 as already agreed; playground, if it ships, $5/day with a 503 and a static sample at 80%. Each harness prints running cost every N calls and exits non-zero at its cap. Set post_tool_additional_context: false in policies/default.yaml for v1 so the nudge is opt-in and measured in the shadow/live arm, and add one Section 8.2 metric: context tax, the mean and p95 additional input tokens per session attributable to Verdict (additionalContext plus block reasons) and the resulting added dollars per session at the user's model price, reported beside Verdict's own provider cost so the published number is the total.

findings.title: Section 15 is load-bearing for the plan's own replay design yet only 15.2 was reviewed, and verdict replay has no acceptance criterion
findings.problem: Section 4.4 justifies recording policy_version and threshold_used on every action precisely because it makes the Section 15 RL extension cheap, and Phase 1 mentions deterministic replay in passing, but no phase defines what replay must reproduce, no test is specified and no metric depends on it, so an agent implements the columns and never builds the replay that is their only purpose. Of the five extensions only 15.2 was reviewed, for training-data licensing; 15.1's bandit fitted on replayed history inherits the same question about deriving a learned artifact from Claude Code session data and was never examined, and 15.3-15.5 were untouched.
findings.evidence: VERDICT_PLAN.md:158 'Every action row records policy_version and threshold_used so you can replay history under a new policy offline (verdict replay --policy new.yaml). This replay capability is what makes the RL extension (Section 15) cheap.'; VERDICT_PLAN.md:383 '1. Learned thresholds (RL/bandits). Treat per-context thresholds as a policy; reward = downstream outcome'
findings.recommendation: Give replay a testable contract in Phase 1: verdict replay --policy <f> --since <date> --json re-evaluates stored answers under a new policy and emits, per action row, old action, new action and the threshold that moved it. Acceptance is a test that replaying the shipped policy over a frozen fixture set reproduces recorded actions byte-for-byte and that changing one YAML threshold changes exactly the rows whose probability straddles it; make that test the gate on the 4.4 columns existing at all. Extend the go/no-go authorization gate written for 15.2 to cover 15.1, since a bandit fitted on replayed Claude Code session outcomes is a learned artifact derived from the same data, and add one line to 15.3-15.5 marking them unreviewed and requiring their own scope and licensing pass, so a later session does not read them as approved backlog.
